statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail sits in the low band well below the block threshold, while Stress stays elevated on the oil-led inflation impulse, a 4.76 percent 10-year yield and hawkish September rate repricing.
recommendation: Conditions remain consistent with a contained, two-sided regime in which mean reversion is functioning: the Nasdaq-100 has traded a full round trip inside its session range rather than holding an extreme. The narrow evidence-based danger window covers the S&P Global Manufacturing PMI, ISM Manufacturing PMI and JOLTS releases on 1 September between 13:45 and 15:00 UTC, where conditional Tail peaks in the watch band. The August month-end cash close at 20:00 UTC today is a secondary checkpoint. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this descriptive assessment.
headline: Nasdaq-100 round-trips its range into the month-end close as crude above $90 and a 4.76 percent 10-year keep Stress elevated
body: The Nasdaq-100 is near 29,402, down about 0.11 percent, after traversing its full 29,304 to 29,465 session range in both directions and settling in the mid-to-upper part of it. That round trip is the central price-path observation: retracements are deep, pullbacks are not unusually shallow, and the index is not pinned to a session extreme. VIX is 15.08, up roughly 4.5 percent but already back off its 15.48 high and low in absolute terms. The broader tape is weaker than the Nasdaq, with the S&P 500 down about 0.40 percent and the Dow about 0.61 percent, so breadth is soft while energy leads and semiconductors hold up. Two macro channels dominate. First, renewed Strait of Hormuz escalation after US strikes on Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island and Iranian retaliation against US facilities in Jordan has lifted WTI about 2.9 percent to roughly 85.80 dollars, with Brent above 90 dollars. Second, that energy impulse is feeding a hawkish rate repricing: the 10-year Treasury yield is up 4 basis points to 4.76 percent, its highest intraday level since January 2025, the 30-year is up 5 basis points to 5.26 percent while the 2-year is broadly unchanged near 4.36 percent, and market-implied odds of a September rate hike have risen to roughly 62 percent from about 40 percent a week ago after Chairman Warsh's 28 August Jackson Hole remarks framed inflation as still too high. Bear steepening of this kind widens the distribution of outcomes, which is why Stress is elevated. Neither channel has yet produced the signature that matters for Tail, so Tail stays low. The identified checkpoints are the August month-end cash close at 20:00 UTC today, where rebalancing imbalances can impose a short directional drift, and the simultaneous ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS releases at 14:00 UTC on 1 September, which carry the clearest mechanism for a repricing leg that could deny retracement.

lookbackSummary: The past 24 hours cover the late Sunday Globex reopen through the US Monday afternoon session. Tail began at 5 with a quiet, orderly regime, rose to 15 around the 00:00 UTC Asian reprice of the Larak Island strikes, eased back to 5 through the European morning, and spiked briefly to 17 at 09:00 UTC on the crude-led inflation impulse before settling between 9 and 13 through the US session. Stress climbed steadily from 29 to 55 as oil, long-end yields and September rate-hike odds all repriced hawkishly. The action mapping stayed EA_ON and green for all 24 hours, because at no point did the assessed price path show the persistent no-retracement structure that raises Tail. Confidence held in the 84 to 88 band throughout on continuously available live price and cross-asset evidence.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours run from the US Monday afternoon through the month-end cash close, the Globex maintenance break, the Asian and European sessions, and into the Tuesday US morning. Conditional Tail eases to 8 during the 21:00 UTC maintenance halt when no price path can form, drifts between 10 and 13 overnight, firms to 13 through the European session, and peaks at 22 in the 14:00 UTC hour on 1 September when ISM Manufacturing PMI and JOLTS Job Openings release simultaneously into an already hawkish rate backdrop. That is the only hour mapped to WATCH and yellow; every other hour remains EA_ON and green. The danger window is deliberately narrow at 13:45 to 15:00 UTC, covering the S&P Global PMI final, the double release and the immediate yield-reaction leg. Stress peaks at 64 in the same hour and decays afterwards on the assumption of orderly price discovery. Confidence decays from 87 to 60 with distance from the last live observation, which is the expected horizon effect rather than an evidence problem.
